overview: A ward-level QI project on Ward 6B using the Model for Improvement: eight weekly baseline points, then three PDSA cycles of about four weeks each that test and refine a structured bedside handoff checklist with a four-line medicines section, supported by fortnightly feedback at the huddle.
population: All nursing shift handoffs at 07:00 and 19:00 for adult inpatients on Ward 6B from September to December 2026; weekly measurement samples 20 handoff sheets chosen by a fixed rota of bed numbers.
exposure: Structured bedside handoff checklist: identity and situation, then medicines (held doses, new high-alert medicines, changes made today, items pending from pharmacy), then pending tasks. Done at the bedside with the patient when awake; for sleeping patients the medicines section is completed at the station.
procedures: Cycle 1 (October): one side of the ward, 19:00 handoff only, paper checklist. Cycle 2 (November): both handoffs on the same side, wording revised from cycle 1 debriefs. Cycle 3 (December): whole ward. At each huddle debrief the team reviews the run chart and two example sheets. The medication safety nurse reviews 20 sheets per week against the medication administration record using a written operational definition; the ward pharmacist double-reviews a random 10 percent.

outcomes.name: Handoffs with at least one missed reconciliation item
outcomes.measure: Weekly proportion of sampled handoff sheets missing a held dose, a new high-alert medicine, a same-day change or a pending pharmacy item that is recorded in the medication administration record
outcomes.why: Directly measures the failure the checklist targets and matches the local baseline definition.

outcomes.name: Checklist completion
outcomes.measure: Proportion of sampled handoffs with every checklist section completed
outcomes.why: Effects fade when completion falls; separates a failed idea from failed delivery.

outcomes.name: Patient participation in the bedside medicines check
outcomes.measure: Proportion of sampled handoffs in which an awake patient took part, reported separately for patients with hearing or cognitive impairment
outcomes.why: Tracks the bedside element and who is left out of it.

outcomes.name: Handoff duration
outcomes.measure: Minutes per patient, timed on two handoffs per week
outcomes.why: The night shift cannot absorb more than about two extra minutes per patient.

outcomes.name: Patients reporting being woken by handoff
outcomes.measure: Yes or no question at the morning medicines round for patients in sampled beds
outcomes.why: Disturbance is the main cost of bedside delivery to patients.

feasibility: Uses the approved 10 minutes of huddle time, the existing handoff sheets and about one hour per week of the medication safety nurse's time for 20 sheets. No electronic record changes are needed.
biasMitigation: Written operational definition of a missed item, with examples, fixed before baseline
Fixed rota of bed numbers for sampling instead of reviewer choice
Pharmacist double review of a random 10 percent of sheets each fortnight
Annotated run chart recording co-interventions such as staffing changes

biasFlags.label: Reviewer expectation
biasFlags.note: The reviewer knows the period; double review and a fixed definition limit drift.

biasFlags.label: Secular trend
biasFlags.note: Other hospital safety work could lower misses; annotate the chart and compare with pharmacist-found discrepancies.

biasFlags.label: Selection of sheets
biasFlags.note: Rota-based sampling avoids choosing easy or complete sheets.

flags: Two process and two balancing measures; no secondary effect claims
parsimony.simplestPath: One ward, one outcome measure on a run chart, three short cycles, existing sheets and huddles.

theoreticalFramework: Model for Improvement with PDSA cycles; SEIPS only to name work-system factors (tasks, tools, environment) when revising the checklist between cycles.
summary: Three PDSA cycles over 12 weeks after an 8-week baseline; one outcome measure, two process and two balancing measures.
